chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him): A man bequeathed a third of his wealth to his male mawali and his female mawali. Are the male and female equal in it, or is there for the male the share of two females from the bequest? So he (peace be upon him) signed: What the deceased bequeathed is valid, upon what he bequeathed, God willing.
ai.seo_question: How is a bequest distributed between male and female mawali in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that a testator’s specific instructions regarding the distribution of one-third of his estate to non-heir clients (mawali) are binding, whether he chooses equal shares for males and females or the traditional male-double-female ratio. Imam al-Hadi (AS) affirms the validity of the deceased's will, highlighting the flexibility in Islamic inheritance law for bequests outside the fixed Quranic shares. This ruling underscores the principle of respecting the testator's intent within the permissible one-third limit.
